description: Unharnessed, unloaded, unled — and still keeping to its route. Get in the way and it comes on at a walk.
lore: In the life it fell out of, somebody owned it. That is not a small thing to know about a creature. It means there was a person who fed it and swore at it and roped things onto its back every morning, and that the donkey came down here, and the person did not come down beside it.

Look at what comes off one. A bronze camp knife on a ribbed grip, made for rope and rations. Braided hemp chewed to a splay at one end. Three iron links worn smooth on the inside where a harness sat for years. A roll of coarse grey canvas. A hide pegged out with little stakes by somebody who began the tanning and gave up on it. The teeth are the animal's own and say only that it chewed all day. Everything else is one person's kit for going somewhere and stopping for the night, and every bit of it is still coming off a donkey that is carrying nothing at all.

One more thing comes out of it, and that one gets underestimated exactly once. It comes up olive and threaded through with root, and there is no fire in it and no appetite, which is what people look for when they weigh a stone in the hand, so the plain ones tend to get set aside. The ones who crack for a living stopped doing that with this one early. Think about what root actually does. A road stays a road because somebody walks it daily; leave off for a season and the verge is up through the middle of it, without hurry, without anything you could call force, and the road loses. That is what a working body presses down to, and carried it does both of the things it always did — closes your own small hurts over while you are busy with something else, and puts the verge into whatever you strike. Nothing about it looks like a weapon. It is nevertheless the sort of thing that takes a wall apart.

Anybody who has met one on a path will say the same. It does not stalk and it does not hold ground. It comes on at a walk, in a line, and the line does not bend around you. You are standing in a route it was walking before the route went soft, and whatever you would take that up with went out of it a long time ago. A working animal does not need much of itself to go on working: a road, a load, and a voice up at the front. It has the road. The load went, and it walks as though it had not. The voice went so long ago that there is no name left to put to it, and the ears have not been told. You will see one halt in open ground with both ears swung forward at nothing whatever, waiting to be spoken to, and then walk on.
